data.narrative:
Neros is a Series B-stage defense and security company founded by Soren Monroe-Anderson and Olaf Hichwa, having raised $121M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of ten comparable companies: eight private firms and two public benchmarks (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). Same-stage, same-sector private peers include Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Defense Unicorns ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression anchors to total capital raised ($121M) and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $230M. Peer-median analysis across the seven same-stage, same-sector private comparables produced a median valuation of $1.0B, with observed range of $300M to $3.0B, reflecting significant dispersion within the cohort.

The two methods yield a triangulated range of $195M (low), $615M (median), and $1.1B (high). The wide gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects material uncertainty in market positioning: stage-progression assumes modest growth from capital-raised proxy, while peer-median suggests Neros may command valuation closer to established sector competitors. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to peers, customer concentration, and defensibility of underlying technology. The median estimate of $615M balances early-stage capital constraints against peer-set benchmarks.
